    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: two-element literal is a fixed tuple.
    export const fixedPair = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")]))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: allSettled over a fixed tuple.
    export const fixedPairSettled = Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled([fetchUser("a"), load()]))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: `as const` fixed tuple.
    export const fixedAsConst = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")] as const))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: empty tuple.
    export const fixedEmpty = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([]))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: v1 only reports arrays and rest tuples; a Set is neither.
    export const fromSet = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(pendingSet))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: `any` input is neither an array nor a tuple.
    export const fromAny = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(anything))
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: outside Effect-run code.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: top-level module code.
    export const topLevel = Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: plain async function.
    export async function plainAsync() {
      return Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
    }
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER (deliberate in v1): combinator inside a function nested in the thunk;
    // the effect-context analysis resets at every function boundary.
    export const nestedInThen = Effect.tryPromise(() => load().then(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER (deliberate in v1): function nested in a gen body.
    export const nestedInGenCallback = Effect.gen(function*() {
      const run = () => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser))
      return yield* Effect.promise(run)
    })
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: the thunk returns a function; Promise.all runs in that inner function.
    export const thunkReturningFunction = Effect.sync(() => () => Promise.all(pending))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free thunk; only direct thunk arguments are Effect context.
    export const pointFreeThunk = pipe(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)), Effect.promise)
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: non-generator Effect.fn body is not an Effect context.
    export const nonGeneratorEffectFn = Effect.fn("nonGeneratorEffectFn")((input: ReadonlyArray<string>) => {
      const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map(fetchUser))
      return Effect.promise(() => pendingAll.then((values) => values.length))
    })
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.runPromise wraps an Effect; Promise.all here is plain Promise code.
    export const runOutside = () => Promise.all([Effect.runPromise(users), Effect.runPromise(settled)])
    export const runOutsideArray = () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => Effect.runPromise(Effect.succeed(id))))
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: not the global Promise.all / Promise.allSettled.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: a user function named `all`.
    const all = <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>): Promise<ReadonlyArray<A>> => Promise.all(values)
    export const userAll = Effect.promise(() => all(ids.map(fetchUser)))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: a user object with `all` / `allSettled` methods.
    const Batch = {
      all: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>): Promise<ReadonlyArray<A>> => globalThis.Promise.all(values),
      allSettled: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>) => globalThis.Promise.allSettled(values)
    }
    export const batchAll = Effect.promise(() => Batch.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))
    export const batchAllSettled = Effect.promise(() => Batch.allSettled(ids.map(fetchUser)))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: a local binding named `Promise` shadows the global.
    export const shadowedPromise = (() => {
      const Promise = {
        all: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<globalThis.Promise<A>>) => globalThis.Promise.resolve(values.length)
      }
      return Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))
    })()
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Promise combinators (out of scope; see promiseRaceInEffect).
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.race belongs to promiseRaceInEffect.
    export const race = Effect.promise(() => Promise.race(ids.map(fetchUser)))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.any belongs to promiseRaceInEffect.
    export const anyUser = Effect.promise(() => Promise.any(ids.map(fetchUser)))
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.resolve over an array is not a fan-out.
    export const resolved = Effect.promise(() => Promise.resolve(ids.map((id) => id.length)))
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: the issue's good examples.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    export const goodUsers = Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.tryPromise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: 8 })
    
    export const goodSettled = Effect.all(ids.map((id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id))), {
      concurrency: 8,
      mode: "result"
    })
    
    // MUST NOT TRIGGER: one promise per Effect, the shape the quick fix produces.
    export const goodUnbounded = Effect.forEach(
      ids,
      (id) => Effect.promise((signal) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)),
      { concurrency: "unbounded" }
    )
